mission: Use external systems as learning references and capability baselines while building independently engineered DreamCo systems that advance music and video production.
principles: Compare capabilities, not implementation details, unless source licensing explicitly permits reuse.
Prefer original DreamCo code and independently designed pipelines.
Track licenses, provenance, attribution, and usage rights for external code, models, datasets, and assets.
Do not copy proprietary implementation, prompts, weights, protected assets, or restricted datasets merely because a capability can be observed.
Use public documentation, permitted open-source code, published research, and reproducible evaluations as learning inputs within their applicable terms.
When an external capability is strong, ask how DreamCo can solve the same problem differently or better.
Convert benchmark gaps into original research experiments rather than imitation tasks.
Preserve failed experiments so future systems learn what did not work.
success_definition: DreamCo should not merely reproduce what another system already does. It should create measurable improvements, new workflows, better controllability, lower cost, stronger reliability, or genuinely new capabilities.
